what_it_does: Modern processors sometimes combine different CPU architectures on a single chip (like x86 and RISC-V together) to balance performance and power. Running different instruction set architectures (ISAs) on the same chip traditionally required separate operating system kernels for each, coordinating through slow message passing. Stramash introduces a 'fused-kernel' operating system that runs a single unified kernel across all ISAs by exploiting the fact that they share coherent memory—the same view of data regardless of which CPU accesses it. This lets the OS share kernel data structures directly and use standard synchronization mechanisms, enabling advanced features like unified virtual memory across all processors.
